eligibility_criteria: Lead applicant must be a legal entity registered in PADOR
Applicants must be non-profit organizations, public bodies, or international organizations
Co-applicants and affiliated entities must meet the same eligibility requirements as lead applicant
Applicants must not be subject to exclusion criteria (early detection and exclusion system)
For 100% co-financing rate: lead applicant must be established in Syria or specific locations defined in Section 2.1.3
Applicants must comply with ethics and values requirements including human rights and anti-corruption standards
technical_requirements: Actions must align with one of four lots: Access to affordable justice, Transitional justice processes, Media freedom and pluralism, or Social cohesion
Actions must target Syria and Syrian communities
Actions must contribute to sustainable and equitable development and full enjoyment of human rights
Actions must include monitoring, documentation, and reporting mechanisms
Actions must promote inclusive participation, particularly of women and marginalized groups
Actions must integrate cross-cutting issues: environmental/climate change, gender equality, disability rights, minority rights, youth engagement
Actions must include capacity building and awareness-raising components
required_documents: Concept note (Annex A.1 – Grant application form - Concept note)
Full application (Annex A.2 – Grant application form – Full application) - only for pre-selected applicants
Organization statutes demonstrating establishment under national law
Supporting documents as requested by contracting authority for eligibility verification
Evidence of co-applicant and affiliated entity eligibility
evaluation_criteria: Relevance of the action (20 points maximum): consistency with call objectives, relevance to country/region/sector needs, clarity of target groups and beneficiaries, added-value elements
Design of the action (25 points maximum): intervention logic, context analysis, risks and assumptions, indicative activities, cross-cutting issues integration
Implementation capacity (to be evaluated in full application)
Cost-effectiveness and budget justification (to be evaluated in full application)
Sustainability and impact potential (to be evaluated in full application)
key_constraints: Deadline for concept note submission: 18 May 2026, 12:00 Brussels time
Lot 1 (Access to affordable justice): EUR 2,000,000 fixed grant amount
Lot 2 (Transitional justice): EUR 2,000,000 fixed grant amount
Lot 3 (Media freedom): EUR 675,000 fixed grant amount
Lot 4 (Social cohesion): EUR 4,000,000 fixed grant amount
Minimum co-financing: 70% of total eligible costs
Maximum EU co-financing: 90% of total eligible costs (or 100% if lead applicant established in Syria)
Balance must be financed from sources other than EU general budget or European Development Fund
This is a restricted call for proposals (two-stage process: concept note then full application)
Online submission via PROSPECT system is mandatory
requirements.submission_format: Online submission via PROSPECT system (mandatory). Applicants must register in PADOR first.

output.headline: EU €675k fixed grant for media freedom & pluralism in Syria; two-stage restricted CFP via PROSPECT; deadline 18 May 2026.
fit_reasoning: CSIM's core mandate — independent journalism training, editorial coaching, journalist protection across Syrian governorates — maps directly onto Lot 3 priorities 1 and 2 (strengthening independent media, protecting journalists/bloggers/media workers).

Multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production plus information-integrity programming aligns with Lot 3 priority 3 (public awareness on media freedom centrality) and the call's cross-cutting inclusion requirements.

Operational bases in Istanbul, Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli provide credible in-country and near-country reach into Northwest Syria, Northeast Syria, and diaspora newsrooms — directly relevant to the call's Syria-wide geographic scope.

Vetted Syrian journalist network and sub-million-EUR grant delivery track record (SIDA 2021-2024, Internews subaward 2023) demonstrate EU-adjacent donor compliance and reporting capacity against comparable frameworks.
KPMG Türkiye clean audit 2024 satisfies the financial-management credibility bar the EC evaluates at full-application stage; no audit qualifications removes a common disqualifier.

Syrian-led nonprofit status is a strong added-value differentiator: the call explicitly prioritises Syrian civil society as a partner and the background section frames Syrian-led action as central to EU re-engagement strategy.

gap_analysis.gap: PADOR registration is in progress but not yet complete; PROSPECT submission requires active PADOR registration.
gap_analysis.fix: Prioritise PADOR completion immediately; allow 2-4 weeks for EC validation. Target completion by end of March 2026 to leave buffer before the 18 May 2026 deadline.

gap_analysis.gap: CSIM is registered in Türkiye, not Syria; the 100% co-financing rate is available only to lead applicants established in Syria (per Corrigendum No. 1). At 90% max EU share, CSIM must source 10% co-financing (~€75k) from non-EU funds.
gap_analysis.fix: Identify and commit a co-financing source (e.g. SIDA follow-on, Free Press Unlimited bridge, or in-kind from a co-applicant) before concept note submission; document it in the budget narrative.

gap_analysis.gap: No EU-registered co-applicant is currently identified; the call rewards consortium proposals and CSIM's appetite for a JV partner is confirmed but no partner is named.
gap_analysis.fix: Identify an EU-eligible co-applicant (e.g. a European press-freedom NGO or media-development INGO with PADOR registration) within 4 weeks; formalise a partnership agreement before full-application stage.

gap_analysis.gap: Past performance is entirely sub-million-EUR; Lot 3 is a fixed €675k grant, which is within range, but the EC may scrutinise whether CSIM has managed a single grant of this size as lead applicant (vs. subaward recipient).
gap_analysis.fix: In the concept note and full application, clearly distinguish lead-applicant grants (SIDA) from subawards (Internews); quantify total managed budget across the portfolio to demonstrate aggregate capacity.

gap_analysis.gap: No explicit evidence of cross-cutting gender-equality or disability-rights programming in CSIM's profile, which is a scored criterion in the evaluation grid.
gap_analysis.fix: Document existing gender-disaggregated beneficiary data and any women-journalist-specific programming; if thin, design a dedicated gender component into the Lot 3 action.

red_flags: PADOR registration incomplete: if not resolved before submission, the application is administratively invalid regardless of technical quality.
Fixed grant amount (EUR 675,000) with no flexibility — budget must be engineered precisely to this ceiling; under- or over-budgeting is not possible.

CSIM is Türkiye-registered, not Syria-registered; evaluators may weight Syria-established applicants more favourably for the 100% co-financing rate optic, even though Türkiye-based organisations are eligible.
No named EU-eligible co-applicant identified yet; consortium-building under time pressure risks weak partnership agreements that evaluators penalise.
conditions_for_bid: Complete PADOR registration and obtain active status before end of March 2026.
Identify and formalise a partnership agreement with at least one EU-eligible co-applicant (European press-freedom or media-development NGO with active PADOR profile) within 4 weeks of bid decision.
Secure a written co-financing commitment of at least EUR 67,500 from a non-EU source (e.g. SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, or in-kind contribution) before concept note submission.
next_steps: IMMEDIATE (this week): Escalate PADOR registration to highest internal priority; assign a dedicated staff member to complete all fields and upload required documents; target submission to EC by 28 February 2026.

WEEK 1-2: Map and shortlist 3-5 potential EU-eligible co-applicants (e.g. Reporters Without Borders, Index on Censorship, Free Press Unlimited as lead-level partner, or a European university media centre); initiate partnership conversations.
WEEK 2-3: Confirm co-financing source and obtain a letter of commitment; document in a one-page co-financing memo for the bid file.

WEEK 3-4: Register for the online information session on 21 April 2026 (email DELEGATION-SYRIA-FCA@eeas.europa.eu by 15 April 2026; max two participants); use session to clarify any Section 2.1.3 geographic eligibility questions.

WEEK 4-6: Draft concept note (Annex A.1) with intervention logic focused on Lot 3 priorities 1-3; integrate gender and cross-cutting components; internal review against the 20+25 point evaluation grid before submission.

output.tender_type_note: Restricted CFP (concept note → full application); quality-scored; fixed grant amount; PROSPECT submission mandatory.

notes: Fixed grant amount for Lot 3: exactly EUR 675,000 — no negotiation on grant size.
EU co-financing maximum for Türkiye-registered lead applicant: 90% (EUR 607,500); co-financing floor: 10% (EUR 67,500) from non-EU sources.
Minimum EU co-financing share: 70% of total eligible costs.
Balance (co-financing) must not come from the EU general budget or European Development Fund.

Two-stage process: concept note evaluated first; full application (including detailed budget) only requested from pre-selected applicants — avoid investing full budget-build effort before pre-selection.
No performance bond, bid security, or retention terms stated in the guidelines; standard EC grant contract terms (PRAG) will apply at contracting stage.
